content.title: About
content.content: Pancakes are thin, round flatbreads made from a liquid batter cooked on a skillet. Traditionally they are prepared with wheat flour, eggs, milk, and a small amount of sugar. Pancakes can be served sweet or savory, often topped or filled with a variety of ingredients.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Pancakes are known worldwide under different names: French crêpes, Russian blini, Ethiopian injera.
In Russia, pancakes are a central part of Maslenitsa, a festival marking the end of winter.
The largest pancake ever made was over 15 meters in diameter, cooked in the United States in 2012.
Pancake contests often feature creative fillings such as seafood, chocolate, or exotic fruits.
There are more than 30 batter variations, including buckwheat, oat, and gluten‑free versions.

items.title: Source of carbohydrates
items.content: Pancakes provide quick‑release energy thanks to the carbohydrates in the batter.

items.title: Contains protein
items.content: Eggs and milk add a modest amount of complete protein to the dish.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: Wheat flour and milk supply B1, B2, and niacin, which support metabolism.

items.title: Minerals
items.content: Pancakes provide calcium, iron, and magnesium, beneficial for bones and nerves.

items.title: Dietary flexibility
items.content: The recipe can be adapted with whole‑grain flour, plant‑based milk, or egg substitutes to meet various dietary needs.

items.title: Gluten allergy
items.content: Traditional wheat‑flour pancakes may trigger reactions in people with celiac disease or gluten sensitivity.

items.title: High glycemic index
items.content: Pancakes can cause a rapid rise in blood sugar, which is important for individuals with diabetes to monitor.

items.title: Fat content
items.content: Cooking with oil can increase the fat content; using a small amount of oil or a non‑stick pan reduces this.

items.title: Additives
items.content: Some ready‑mix pancake mixes contain preservatives and additives that may be undesirable for sensitive consumers.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Serve pancakes hot, rolled or folded. They can be brushed with butter, drizzled with honey, jam, or sour cream, and filled with meat, fish, cheese, vegetables, or fruit. For a lighter option, use whole‑grain or gluten‑free flour.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store cooked pancakes in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 3 days. They can also be frozen in a stack separated by parchment paper and reheated in a microwave or skillet.
